We need answer extract claims per schema. Need parse review. Need output JSON only? User provides format. Need extract product-review semantic claims. Review title Nope, source: "Nope\nSo these charge great  ... but what I’ve realized is that they give off a really high pitched white noise sound . I thought I was going crazy , but then realized the noise was coming from charger . Maybe I have sensitive ears , but it’s pretty annoying."

Need identify claims. Product likely charger? Claims:
1 positive charging performance: "these charge great" primary function_performance secondary charging_success? Or general_performance? They charge great = charging success/performance. taxonomy function_performance includes charging_success, charging_speed, power_output, protection_effectiveness, general_performance. "charge great" likely charging_success positive. Evidence exact substring "these charge great" maybe "So these charge great"? Need exact continuous substring from SOURCE_TEXT. Include "So these charge great" maybe.
2 abnormal noise: high pitched white noise sound coming from charger, annoying. Primary safety_risk? secondary abnormal_noise. Polarity negative. Evidence span exact: "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound" or full "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound ." Need exact continuous substring. The source has "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound ." Note space before period? It says "sound . I thought". So exact substring can be "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound" without period. Also "the noise was coming from charger" supports source. But one claim can use entire: "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound . I thought I was going crazy , but then realized the noise was coming from charger . Maybe I have sensitive ears , but it’s pretty annoying." But evidence_span should be exact continuous. Could choose "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound" enough. Polarity negative. Primary safety_risk secondary abnormal_noise. Also annoyance maybe not needed.

Need ensure no other claims. Maybe "charge great" positive. "Nope" title? Not semantic product claim? no.

Need output JSON with claims array. Exactly schema. Need no markdown? likely JSON.

Need decide primary/secondary for charge great. Could be function_performance/charging_success. Evidence_span "these charge great" exact? Source: "So these charge great  ... but". There is "these charge great" yes. That's continuous. Polarity positive. However "charge great" maybe general performance. But charging_success is valid if they charge successfully. "great" indicates success. Use charging_success.

Potential issue: "these charge great" refers to chargers? Yes.

Abnormal noise. Primary safety_risk because abnormal_noise under safety_risk. Secondary abnormal_noise. Polarity negative. Evidence_span: "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound" exact. The source says "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound ." If we don't include period okay exact substring from before period. It is continuous. Good.

Need maybe include "Maybe I have sensitive ears , but it’s pretty annoying." for negative? But evidence should focus noise. Negative because annoying. Could include "it’s pretty annoying" as evidence? But claim about noise, need evidence span could be "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound" enough; polarity negative from annoying not in span? The claim polarity determined by semantic. It's okay.

Should we have mixed? "charge great but noise annoying" separate claims. Each polarity independent. So positive and negative.

Return JSON. Ensure valid JSON. Use curly apostrophe? Source uses "what I’ve" etc. We don't need. Use exact substring "these charge great" and "they give off a really high pitched white noise sound". Good.

Need check "exactly one valid primary/secondary taxonomy pair". primary safety_risk + secondary abnormal_noise valid. primary function_performance + secondary charging_success valid.

Output:
{"claims":[{"primary_topic":"function_performance","secondary_topic":"charging_success","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"these charge great"},{"primary_topic":"safety_risk","secondary_topic":"abnormal_noise","polarity":"negative","evidence_span":"they give off a really high pitched white noise sound"}]}

Need no extra.

{"claims":[{"primary_topic":"function_performance","secondary_topic":"charging_success","polarity":"positive","evidence_span":"these charge great"},{"primary_topic":"safety_risk","secondary_topic":"abnormal_noise","polarity":"negative","evidence_span":"they give off a really high pitched white noise sound"}]}
